analysis.investment_thesis: Raymond Lifestyle carries a century-old brand with genuine consumer recognition, but post-demerger financials reveal a business earning almost nothing — ROE of 0.67% and net profit collapsing from INR 2,645 Cr (one-time demerger gains) to INR 38 Cr in FY25. At 50x trailing P/E with rapidly rising debt, this fails my most basic quality and valuation filters.
key_strengths: Strong brand heritage — Raymond, Park Avenue, ColorPlus are genuinely trusted Indian apparel brands with 100+ years of equity
Decent gross margin of 42.46% suggests some pricing power in the branded segment
Promoter holding at 58.22% is stable and above my 55% threshold
key_risks: Earnings collapse is alarming — net profit crashed from INR 2,645 Cr to INR 38 Cr; FY24 was inflated by demerger accounting, not real operating performance
Debt nearly doubled in one year (INR 1,540 Cr → INR 2,290 Cr); finance cost of INR 207 Cr consumes 44% of operating income of INR 470 Cr — interest coverage is dangerously thin at ~2.3x
E-commerce and fast fashion are structurally disrupting branded apparel retail, threatening the company's large store network
red_flags: ROE of 0.67% and ROCE of 2.87% — a business earning less than a savings account on its equity is not a business I will own
Net profit of INR 38 Cr on INR 6,177 Cr revenue = 0.6% net margin — deeply insufficient
EBITDA halved YoY (INR 1,077 Cr → INR 626 Cr) and operating income more than halved (INR 937 Cr → INR 470 Cr) — the underlying business is deteriorating, not recovering
Historical financials (pre-2024) are from a shell entity with INR 107-128 Cr revenue — the demerger makes multi-year trend analysis meaningless
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Raymond Lifestyle was demerged from Raymond Limited in 2024, which makes the historical numbers almost useless for trend analysis — the pre-2024 entity was a stub. What we can see in FY25 is troubling: revenue of INR 6,177 Cr generated only INR 38 Cr of net profit. The INR 2,645 Cr profit in FY24 was a demerger accounting artefact, not operating performance. Meanwhile, total debt jumped from INR 1,540 Cr to INR 2,290 Cr in a single year — exactly the kind of debt-funded expansion I avoid. Finance costs of INR 207 Cr against operating income of only INR 470 Cr leaves the company with almost no cushion. ROE of 0.67% on an equity base of INR 9,646 Cr is simply unacceptable.

The brand itself has real value — Raymond is one of India's oldest and most trusted apparel names — and the 42% gross margin shows consumers will pay for it. But brand alone does not make a good investment. Operating margins of 7.82% are at the floor of my comfort zone, and the forward P/E of 15x only makes sense if the company can achieve ~INR 325 Cr net profit — nearly 9x FY25 earnings — which requires a dramatic operational turnaround I have no evidence is coming. I want steady, boring compounders with fortress balance sheets. This is a restructuring story with uncertain earnings, rising leverage, and a P/E of 50x. I will pass and watch from the sidelines.
